text:
mira: ap-northeast1 ALB healthchecks for edge-proxy are flapping — IPv4 probes succeed, IPv6 probes time out. Started ~02:30 UTC. Anyone seen ALB v6 healthcheck oddness?

sam: which LB type? ALB (application) or NLB?

mira: ALB (app/alb-edge), target type = instance (nodeport). health check path /_hc -> 200 normally. from bastion: v4 curl -> 200 OK, v6 curl -> connection timed out.

alex: can you tcpdump on a node to capture the probe packets + replies?

mira: pasted snippets:
```
$ kubectl get svc edge-proxy -n edge
NAME        TYPE       CLUSTER-IP       EXTERNAL-IP  PORT(S)          AGE
edge-proxy  NodePort   10.10.123.45     <nodes>       8080:32080/TCP    3d
```
```
# from bastion
$ curl -4 -v http://10.0.12.34:32080/_hc
> HTTP/1.1 200 OK

$ curl -6 -v http://[2a05:xxxx:xxxx::1]:32080/_hc
* Rebuilt URL to: http://[2a05:xxxx:xxxx::1]:32080/_hc
*   Trying 2a05:xxxx:xxxx::1...
* connect to 2a05:xxxx:xxxx::1 port 32080 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to 2a05:xxxx:xxxx::1 port 32080: Connection timed out
```

```
# tcpdump on node (shortened)
12:31:05.123456 IP6 2a05:7b40::abcd > 2600:1fff:xxxx::node: TCP S 42342 > 32080
# node never sends RST or SYN-ACK
```

# aws nacl describe (trimmed)
```
- RuleNumber: 50  Allow  IPv4  0.0.0.0/0
- RuleNumber: 100 Deny   IPv6  ::/0    <-- universal deny for IPv6 inbound
```

sam: that DENY on IPv6 explains it — IPv4 path was allowed, IPv6 blocked at NACL. Remember NACLs are stateless: inbound denial will drop ALB probe or block the return flow for ephemeral source ports.

mira: weird: why do we only see healthcheck failures and not other v6 traffic to nodes?

alex: a couple of possible reasons: ALB healthchecks come from specific ALB IP ranges and use ephemeral source ports; other v6 traffic may hit different SG/NACL combos or go via different subnets. Also we use NAT for IPv4 egress, but IPv6 flows are native so NACL matters more.

sam: short remedial options: (1) add a specific allow rule for ALB v6 source CIDR (lookup via describe-load-balancers -> sourceIp), inserted with a lower rule number than the deny, or (2) narrow/remove the blanket ::/0 deny and replace with explicit denies. Both work; prefer targeted allow + rule ordering.

mira: i pushed an allow at rule 60 for the ALB v6 prefix and re-applied.

oncall-bot: Config change applied by mira at 02:47 UTC: network-acl acl-0abcde updated (added allow rule 60 for 2a05:xxxx:xxxx::/32).

mira: after change ALB healthchecks show healthy in console, verified targets now healthy across nodepool (checked timestamp 02:49).

alex: please add an audit to scan other regions for IPv6 blanket denies in NACLs — we should avoid wide ::/0 denies that unintentionally block platform-managed LB probes.

mira: created INFRA-2437 to audit NACLs + add a CI check to exercise ALB healthchecks over v6 for new infra changes.

deploy-bot: INFRA-CHK job queued to run in 10m to validate healthchecks across regions.

sam: nice find, thanks. :thumbsup:
